findings.reasoning: In Tailwind CSS, combining `w-full` with `max-w-4xl` and `lg:max-w-5xl` sets a fluid width (`width: 100%`) with an upper bound (`max-width: 56rem` and `max-width: 64rem` on desktop). It does not impose a minimum or fixed width. On mobile viewports (e.g. 375px–430px), the element scales to 100% of the container width without exceeding the viewport bounds, preventing horizontal overflow or scrollbar physics degradation. Under the presumption of correctness and CSS layout specifications, no layout overflow defect exists.

Both the header section and the main content body container enforce identical horizontal layout constraints: 'max-w-xl mx-auto w-full px-5'. Neither container defines divergent breakpoint-specific width or padding overrides (e.g., md:max-w-2xl or sm:px-6), ensuring strict horizontal alignment parity and gutter consistency across all viewports. Additionally, the outer wrapper enforces 'overflow-x-hidden overscroll-x-none', preventing horizontal shifts.

Static review of the component reveals that the profile view container is constrained to `max-w-xl mx-auto w-full px-5` without any responsive expansion to `max-w-4xl` or `max-w-5xl`. Furthermore, interactive action buttons are explicitly sized at `w-11 h-11` (44x44px, meeting WCAG 2.5.5 targets), and row items have generous padding (`p-4`). Scaling does not dynamically shrink or degrade touch targets on larger viewports. The reported issue is unsubstantiated.
